examShortTricks: Trick 1: Politics passages use loaded language — separate FACT from OPINION; comprehension questions ask you to identify the writer's stance, so track evaluative words.
Trick 2: 'Power corrupts' essay: define → one historical example → one modern example → safeguard (accountability, free press) — structure beats rhetoric.
Trick 3: In debate-style answers, pre-empt the opposition: 'Some argue... however...' — acknowledging the other side is the top-band move.
practiceQuestions: Q. How can power be kept in check? Suggest two ways. (2 marks) — independent judiciary/media; periodic free elections.
Q. Why do people abuse power? (2 marks) — lack of accountability and human greed; give one example.
keyPoints: Distinguish power (capacity) from authority (legitimate right) in definitions.
Analyse how texts show power misuse — through a character's decision, not description.
